name: Pixel Art
traits: visible square pixels on one fixed low-resolution grid
tile-based rooms and snappy low-frame-count motion
suits: games, apps, gadgets and snacks; playful, nostalgic, tech-savvy brands
stylePara: Pixel art at a low native resolution, scaled up with hard nearest-neighbour edges: every form is made of visible square pixels on one fixed grid, about 180 pixels across the frame; a restrained palette of 16 to 24 colours, with ordered dithering for gradients and hue-shifted shadows that turn cooler and more saturated as they darken; hand-placed one-pixel outlines darker than the fill; characters are compact sprites with large heads; no anti-aliasing, no blur, no smooth gradients; sets are tile-based rooms with a clear floor line.

rendering.line: one-pixel hand-placed outlines a shade darker than the fill, lighter on lit edges
rendering.shading: two or three flat value steps per material, ordered dithering between them, hue-shifted shadows
rendering.colour: fixed 16-24 colour palette shared by the whole film; product colours mapped to the nearest palette entries
rendering.texture: the pixel grid itself; tiles repeat visibly on floors and walls
rendering.lighting: a consistent light side baked into the sprites; no dynamic light or glow

motion: Sprite animation with few drawings: 4-8 frame cycles held on threes or fours (about 6-8 drawings per second), everything moves in whole-pixel steps, idle bobs of one pixel; no sub-pixel smoothing, no tweening, no motion blur.
camera: Fixed side-on or three-quarter top-down view; the camera scrolls in whole-pixel steps or cuts between rooms; no zooms and no rotation, which break the grid.
avoid: the pixel grid melting or resampling during motion
mixed pixel sizes in one frame
pixel glyphs that read as fake text
sheets: Each character as a sprite sheet: front, side and back idle frames plus a 4-frame walk, on a flat background, with the palette listed and the sprite height in pixels stated in the prompt; places as tile-based room screens; the product as a small sprite with its colours mapped to the palette.
risk: The hardest style here for Seedance: a video model works in continuous space, so the grid melts, pixel sizes mix and motion slides smoothly between positions. Keep the camera locked, motion small and clips 3-5 s; then in post downsample each frame to the target grid (nearest-neighbour), re-quantise to the palette and step the timing to threes, which restores most of the look. For hero shots, consider animating the approved sprites in code instead.

example.prompt: Pixel art still at a low native resolution with hard square pixels: a compact sprite of a woman in her thirties with a large head, a dark pixel bun and an orange top holds a tiny green glass bottle with a yellow cap, standing in a sunny tile-based kitchen with a clear floor line; a droopy pixel fern sags on the windowsill; a 20-colour palette, ordered dithering in the sunlight patch, hue-shifted shadows, one-pixel dark outlines, no anti-aliasing. Vertical 9:16. No text.
